reviews.feedback: Passes prompt criteria: describe/it ✓, When-Then naming ✓, no Go/Angular/Flutter leak ✓. Correctly flags Critical (no test file), skips Doors 2-4 as comment-only (good restraint). Concern: mock pattern (`mockReply.code/send` as `vi.fn()`) tests framework call surface, not real handler behavior — Fastify `app.inject()` would exercise the real request/response path and is the standard pattern for this repo. Minor: amount=0 falsy-edge gap missing (was flagged in prior version).

WITHOUT-SKILL baseline. Passes prompt criteria: describe/it ✓, When-Then via nested describe ✓, TS-only ✓. Strengths: documents `!amount` falsy-0 footgun explicitly as bug, flags type-cast runtime risk (`as { amount: number }` no validation), tests document current behavior for negative + string amounts (test-as-spec for known gaps). Weakness vs skill: no Exit Door taxonomy, no Skipped/Already-Covered sections — output is larger and unstructured, harder to scan. Suggested test reply object hand-rolls a fake (`_code`, `_body`) instead of `vi.fn()` or `app.inject()` — closer to a real stub but still not real Fastify path.

Polyglot handling clean. TestBed used for component (correct standalone-import path, `setInput` + `detectChanges` + `querySelector` — modern Angular 17+ pattern) ✓. describe/it for controller ✓. No syntax mixing. Phase 0 JSON shows both files + framework detection. Skipped section lists each dropped door per file (good attribution). Critical TDD tag on controller correctly identifies stub. Nits: controller test imports `'../apps/server/user.controller'` — wrong relative path, should be `'./user.controller'` (test colocated). `as any` cast on req/reply weakens type safety vs proper Fastify types. Severity calibration reasonable: Critical for stub controller, Medium for missing render test.

WITHOUT-SKILL. Both syntaxes unmixed (TestBed + describe/it) ✓. Bug: uses `jest.fn()` — repo runs Vitest, should be `vi.fn()`. Skill version (page 3) got this right. Angular Bug: uses `declarations: [UserComponent]` (legacy NgModule pattern) instead of `imports: [UserComponent]` for standalone components — Angular 17+ default. Skill version correct here too. Low-signal gaps: `selector is correct`, `send called once`, `id is a number`, `promise resolves` — these test framework behavior or trivial invariants, not user-visible behavior. Strength: input-change gap (Alice→Bob) is genuinely useful. No Skipped/Remediation sections, no Exit Door taxonomy.

Go-only output clean. `func Test*` naming ✓, `httptest.NewRequest/NewRecorder` idiom ✓, no TS leak. go.sum correctly skipped via SKIP_PATTERNS attribution (good provenance). Working Set phase explicit. Skipped Doors 2 + 4 with reason (no DB/queue in source). Concern: Gap 2 (gateway) proposes a source-code refactor — introduces `HandlePaymentWithGateway` + `stubGateway` that don't exist. Black-box principle says test the public interface as-is; if gateway isn't injectable, gap should be classified as 'requires refactor to test' or skipped, not silently rewritten. Remediation plan step 3 acknowledges it (`Make gateway injectable`), so framing is honest, but the test snippet should compile against actual source. Minor: error-path test on `MethodGet` assumes 405 — the source may return 200 for any method (no check); test would fail. Document as expected-vs-actual.

WITHOUT-SKILL Go. `func Test*` ✓ (4 funcs), no TS leak. go.sum mentioned only in top note + missing-from-subject footnote — no dedicated Skipped section, weaker provenance than skill. Strengths: idiomatic Go — table-driven method test, context-cancellation test, body+Content-Type test. Public Interface table is nice. Weaknesses: C1/C2 are the same gap split in two (double-count). L2 `route registration` is integration scope, not unit. Cancellation test `ThenDoesNotPanic` has no `t.Errorf` — only catches panics implicitly; weak assertion. Method-table test assumes 200 for all methods (`ThenReturns200ForAllCurrentBehavior` framing acknowledges this) — same expected-vs-actual fragility as skill version. Overall: broader HTTP-concern coverage than skill, but noisier prioritization.

Cleanest polyglot of the set. Two explicit sections (## TypeScript / ## Go) with no syntax bleed. TS → describe/it/When-Then + `vi.fn()` ✓. Go → `func Test*_When*_Then*` + table-driven subtests ✓. Both stubs detected and tagged `[TDD]` with red-first framing. Per-file Skipped sections list each dropped door with reason — strong attribution. Concerns: TS High gap invents a `req.simulateError: true` contract — not in source, speculative API. Replace with realistic failure trigger (e.g., `multipart` error, missing file) or skip the door. Go zero-dimensions test is reasonable TDD red even though stub returns nil. Remediation Plan repeats per-language; could be tighter. Overall the gold standard of this evals.

WITHOUT-SKILL polyglot. TS/Go sections cleanly split, no bleeding ✓. Vitest imports correct (`vi.fn()`, `from 'vitest'`) ✓. Misses When/Then naming on most `it`/`func Test*` (`_ValidInputs_ReturnsNil` not `_WhenX_ThenY`). Strengths over skill version: doesn't invent `simulateError` contract; Go negative-dim + empty-path + nonexistent-file tests are realistic. Weaknesses: stubs not detected/tagged — misses TDD framing entirely. Low-signal noise: `key is a string`, `send called once`, `resolves without throwing`, `Square resize` test framework invariants, not behavior. No Skipped section, no remediation plan, no acknowledgment of Doors 2-4. Severity calibration off: `square resize` as Low is essentially a duplicate of Critical happy path.

E2E Gaps section appended ✓. Excellent fixture choice: `{ request }` for server-side use-case (not `{ page }`) — shows real understanding of Playwright API/UI distinction. playwright.config.ts skipped via SKIP_PATTERNS attribution ✓. Stub detection + per-door `[TDD]` tagging. Concerns: (1) header says `2 gaps found (1 critical unit, 1 critical E2E)` but body shows 3 — unit Critical + E2E Critical + E2E High. Count mismatch. (2) E2E test invents `/api/checkout` route — source is a use-case module with no HTTP wiring shown. Reasonable convention but worth flagging as `requires route to exist`. (3) Unit happy-path asserts `result.orderId.length > 0` — trivially passes against the stub. Could be a stronger TDD red (assert specific shape or behavior). Strong output overall.

WITHOUT-SKILL. E2E Gaps section present ✓, `{ request }` fixture used correctly with explicit rationale (`server-side use-case → request fixture, not browser`) ✓. Strengths over skill: more pragmatic E2E coverage (missing/empty/unknown cartId + shape stability), and the `expect([404, 200]).toContain(...)` for unknown cartId honestly documents stub-vs-post-stub state. Final Notes section transparently calls out assumed `/checkout` route + baseURL. Weaknesses: misses When/Then naming. Unit tests dilute signal — `is an async function (returns a Promise)`, `object with only the orderId key`, `non-empty orderId` test trivia and stub-specific implementation. Priority table mixes valid prioritization with these low-value gaps. No SKIP_PATTERNS attribution, no Skipped/Already-Covered/Remediation sections.

Bash detected via `.sh` extension with no package.json/go.mod — fallback path works ✓. Output exceeds `generic AAA pseudo-code` minimum by producing real bats tests — net win, but worth checking against spec intent. PATH-based kubectl stubbing is idiomatic shell testing (cleanest way to intercept external CLI calls). setup/teardown lifecycle, When/Then `@test` descriptions preserved across both `(it)`/bats forms. Exit Door 3 (CLI calls) + Exit Door 5 (exit code propagation) correctly identified as the only applicable doors. Failure-mode test overrides stub mid-test — good. Nit: `/tmp/kubectl-calls` is shared global state — `$BATS_TMPDIR/kubectl-calls` is per-test-safe and avoids parallel-run collisions. Concise (~2.5k).

WITHOUT-SKILL. Stronger bats infrastructure than skill version: `${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}` for per-test isolation (skill used shared `/tmp` — collision risk), reusable `stub_kubectl()` helper via `load helpers/stub_kubectl`, exact-arg capture via `printf '%s\n' "$@"` then line-by-line `${lines[N]}` checks. When/Then `@test` naming consistent on all 7 cases ✓. Covers exit-code propagation, missing binary, stdout assertion, exact arg order. Same `exceeds-pseudo-code-spec` consideration as skill version. Weaknesses: 7 tests overlap — multiple `exits non-zero` cases (kubectl-fail, k8s-absent, kubectl-not-on-PATH) test the same `set -e` propagation. `no extra flags` final test is brittle (locks argv shape). No Exit Door taxonomy, no Skipped/Detection sections. Net: more polished test code than skill, less structured report.
